references.text: Isaiah's prophecy of the suffering servant describes how the Messiah would be despised, mocked, and dishonored—fulfilled in what Jesus predicts here about being ridiculed and mistreated. [ref: Isa 53:3-5|Isaiah 53:3-5]

The prophecy that the Lord's servant offers his back to those who strike him and his cheeks to those who tear out his beard, and does not hide his face from shame and spitting—a direct parallel to Jesus' words about being spat upon. [ref: Isa 50:6|Isaiah 50:6]
Jesus' parallel prediction in the Gospel of Matthew that the Son of Man will be handed over to the Gentiles to be mocked, flogged, and crucified. [ref: Matt 20:18-19|Matthew 20:18-19]
Mark's parallel account where Jesus predicts he will be handed over to the Gentiles, mocked, spat upon, flogged, and killed. [ref: Mark 10:33-34|Mark 10:33-34]
The fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy: The soldiers mocked him, placed a crown of thorns on his head, spat on him, and struck him. [ref: Mark 15:16-20|Mark 15:16-20]
The fulfillment in Matthew: Roman soldiers (the Gentiles) mocked, spat upon, and mistreated Jesus before the crucifixion. [ref: Matt 27:27-31|Matthew 27:27-31]
Herod and his soldiers mock and ridicule Jesus—part of the fulfillment that he was handed over to the Gentiles and dishonored. [ref: Luke 23:11|Luke 23:11]
The soldiers mocked Jesus while he hung on the cross, fulfilling his prediction about being ridiculed by the Gentiles. [ref: Luke 23:36-37|Luke 23:36-37]
Peter's Pentecost sermon confirms that Jesus was handed over according to God's set purpose and foreknowledge, and was killed by the hands of lawless men (the Gentiles). [ref: Acts 2:23|Acts 2:23]
The messianic psalm describes how the suffering one is mocked, ridiculed, and despised by people—a prophetic foreshadowing of Jesus' suffering. [ref: Ps 22:7-9|Psalm 22:7-9]
